## How it works

- [statement] Configured policies constrain execution; when no policy of a given type applies, the corresponding action remains unrestricted. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/agentengine/manage/governance/policy-engine.md

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] MongoDB describes Agent Engine retrieval as powered by Voyage AI, including embeddings and reranking; Codesprint repeats that vendor description rather than reporting an independent benchmark. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-30) — https://www.mongodb.com/company/newsroom/press-releases/mongodb-launches-atlas-agent-engine-to-put-ai-agents-in-production-without-a-new-stack · keywords: Agent Engine feature set: tools, retrieval and guardrails · also: https://www.codesprintconsulting.com/blog/mongodb-atlas-agent-engine-memory-governance
- [statement] The documented content guardrail type is limited to `output_validation`, with regular-expression matching rather than an enumerated general-purpose safety-classifier suite. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/agentengine/manage/governance/guardrails.md
- [statement] Codesprint recommends retrieving action-driving transactional state from its authoritative system immediately before a decision or write; this is application design advice rather than an Agent Engine default. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-30) — https://www.codesprintconsulting.com/blog/mongodb-atlas-agent-engine-memory-governance
- [statement] MongoDB presents Agent Engine retrieval as powered by Voyage AI embeddings and reranking; Lemon Web repeats this description. These sources describe the feature, rather than independently measuring retrieval accuracy. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-29) — https://www.mongodb.com/company/newsroom/press-releases/mongodb-launches-atlas-agent-engine-to-put-ai-agents-in-production-without-a-new-stack · keywords: Agent Engine feature set: tools, retrieval and guardrails · also: https://www.lemon-web.net/lemon-blog/web-development/mongodb-atlas-agent-engine-aims-to-take-ai-agents-from-experiments-into-real-production

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Agent Engine discovers tools from configured remote MCP servers at startup and exposes them to agent code. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/agentengine/add-features/remote-mcp.md
- [statement] Agent code routes tool and model calls through `app.tool(...)` and `app.llm(...)` wrappers for auditing, policy enforcement and replay. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/agentengine/reference/agent-contract.md
- [statement] The guardrail configuration exposes `llm_input` and `llm_output` stages, and `block`, `modify`, `log_only`, and `require_review` actions. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/agentengine/manage/governance/guardrails.md
- [statement] Policy Engine allowlists restrict which tools and models an agent can call. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/agentengine/manage/governance/policy-engine.md
- [statement] A project with no effective policies runs without Policy Engine restrictions; policy enforcement should not be assumed to imply a preconfigured deny policy. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/agentengine/manage/governance/policy-engine.md
- [statement] The documented remote MCP transport is Streamable HTTP; the configuration schema identifies `streamable_http` as the only supported transport value. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/agentengine/add-features/remote-mcp.md
- [statement] Content guardrails and action policies are separate: guardrails inspect model content, while policies govern actions such as tool and model invocation. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/agentengine/manage/governance/guardrails.md · keywords: Agent Engine feature set: tools, retrieval and guardrails · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/agentengine/manage/governance/policy-engine.md
- [statement] The policy engine supports tool-name and tool-catalog allowlisting; a catalog allowance also covers tools added to that catalog later. Custom tools without a catalog match by name. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/agentengine/manage/governance/policy-engine.md
- [statement] Duration and token caps are checkpoint controls: a call can exceed the cap, and concurrent executions can collectively overshoot a session token cap. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/agentengine/manage/governance/policy-engine.md
- [statement] Biagolini explicitly excludes guardrails and custom-tool construction from the hands-on walkthrough; it supplies no implementation validation for those features. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://medium.com/@biagolini/how-to-deploy-your-first-ai-agent-on-mongodb-atlas-agent-engine-powered-by-amazon-bedrock-85a7ca4628b6
